# Sync the hub's documents with their sources

The hub's documents are the source of truth for the factory, so they must stay true to
the material they came from. You re-read sources, show what changed, and edit the
documents only with the user's approval. Never commit; the user does.

Arguments: source ids (`S-003 S-007`), `--stale` (only sources older than
`docs.stale_days`), `--jobs` (Docs impact of merged jobs), or nothing (every active
source that can change: not `prompt`, `file` or `meeting`).

## 1. Re-read

Run `factory/bin/docs list` and pick the sources. Dispatch `researcher` agents (Job A,
a few sources each, in parallel) with the hub path and the ids. Each source comes back
`unchanged`, `changed (material)`, `changed (noise)` or `unreachable`.

Show one table: id, title, result, one-line summary of the change. `unchanged` and
`noise` need nothing more (the snapshot and fetch date are already updated).

## 2. Work out the impact of each material change

For each `changed (material)` source:

1. `factory/bin/docs diff <S-id>`: what changed.
2. `factory/bin/docs cites <S-id>`: every BRD item, spec item, ADR and AGENTS.md line
   that rests on it. Follow one more step: what cites those items (`docs cites BR-004`).
3. For each affected item, decide: still true, needs an edit, or now contradicted.
   An accepted ADR that is contradicted is never rewritten: propose a new ADR that
   supersedes it (`factory/bin/docs adr-new`), and set the old one's Status to
   `Superseded by [ADR-xxxx]`.
4. Check open hub issues and running factory jobs that cite the affected items
   (`gh issue list --label factory --search "<id>"`, `factory/bin/job summary`): they
   may be building against the old rule.

## 3. Agree and apply

Present the proposed edits in grilling format (call the Skill tool with "grilling"):
one numbered question per affected item, showing the current text, the proposed text,
and the source diff it comes from; "yes" accepts. Ask about issues and jobs that are
affected (comment on the issue, give feedback to the job, or leave them).

Apply what the user accepts: edit the documents, keep citations, update `Last
reviewed` dates. Run `factory/bin/docs check` and fix every error. Don't comment on
issues or change jobs without a yes for each.

## --jobs: fold merged work into the documents

For each finished job in `docs/history/` (its `job.json` says `merged`) whose
`decision.md` has a Docs impact other than "None." and that isn't yet listed in
`docs/sources/synced-jobs.json`: read the Docs impact and `spec.md` there (they're in the
hub's git, so this works on any machine), propose the document edits as above (an ADR from the job
moves from Proposed to Accepted), and after applying, append the job id to
`docs/sources/synced-jobs.json` (create it as `{"jobs": []}` if missing).

## 4. Report

What changed upstream, what you updated (document and ids), what you left and why,
unreachable sources and what would fix them, and when each source was last fetched.
